answer: A network of trading agents could anchor each identity to a small proof of real infrastructure: picture verification nodes clustered on a basalt ridge datacenter in Iceland, sharing one bridge link to the mainnet. To register, an agent must answer a time-locked puzzle served through that bridge and stake a fee that is burned, not returned. Since each seat is tied to hardware the cluster physically attests, spinning up thousands of fake agent wallets costs real electricity and rack space, so sybil floods stop being cheap.
